messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 0063 detected: sustained backend GPU queue growth -> elevated tail latency for streaming responses. Auto-alert to #incidents and paging the on-call.
mike_oncall: grabbing. seeing 5xx spike on push-stream gateway and token auth timeouts. latency climbs ~400ms p50 -> 1.8s p95 on streaming endpoints. :eyes:
maya_eng: confirmed. Worker pools for streaming are saturated on eu-west-1. Non-streaming (poll) endpoints look stable. Client retries increasing.
cheng_sre: can we throttle client connections or reduce ingress traffic shape? Suggest temporary stop of streaming feature for non-enterprise customers while we stabilize.
mike_oncall: agree. priority: stop further user impact and avoid cascading queue growth. Proposal:
  1) flip streaming feature to "soft-disabled" for free/standard tiers (return short response + X-Poll-Advice header)
  2) apply emergency rate-limit profile to streaming routes: `rate_limit.streams=20rpm` for all remaining traffic
  3) route enterprise/dedicated customers to dedicated pool (no change)
  4) deploy fix to autoscaler knobs and KV cache pressure mitigation
lisa_support: heads-up: customers on Pro and below will see streaming replaced with immediate non-stream response. We'll need a short advisory message and a support playbook.
samir_prod: notify docs and health page. We should also add a fallback code path in the client SDKs to surface polling suggestion.
maya_eng: readiness: I can patch the config API to set `feature.streaming.enabled=false` for the standard orgs and add a header `X-Redwood-Stream-Fallback: polling` within 3m. Patching now.
ops-bot: Running: POST /internal/config/rollouts
  payload: {"selector":"tier:standard","feature":"streaming","enabled":false}
  status: queued -> applied to 73% of standard orgs
mike_oncall: applying rate limit rule now:
  `rl_command apply --route /v1/stream --policy emergency_throttle_20rpm`
maya_eng: rollout completed for 100% standard orgs. Streaming transport now returns HTTP 200 with `streaming_disabled` hint for existing connections; SDKs should switch to poll.
cheng_sre: monitoring: backend queue length dropping, CPU on streaming-shard-*.prod down 35%, p95 latency improving.
lisa_support: support note drafted:
  - What customers see: streaming will be replaced by a single short response; guidance to re-poll or upgrade to Dedicated for realtime needs.
  - Temporary ETA: 60-120m while we stabilize autoscaler and KV pressure.
  - Escalation: contact on-call in #incidents if any high-severity customer impact.
mike_oncall: paging P1 customers with known realtime SLAs now. cc @lisa_support for customer comms.
incident-bot: Pager update: P1 pages notified: cust-acme, cust-gyro. Priority label set -> "degraded realtime".
samir_prod: posted short advisory on status.redwood.ai: "Temporary reduction of streaming availability for Standard tier to stabilize latency. No changes for Dedicated customers." :loud_sound:
maya_eng: starting autoscaler tuning patch: reduce min_burst=2 -> 1, increase recycle interval, patch rolling update on streaming pods.
cheng_sre: reminder: don't re-enable streaming until p95 < 700ms consistently for 5m and queue < 10 on all shards.
mike_oncall: agreed. plan for gradual canary re-enable to 10% standard orgs after thresholds met.
maya_eng: I'll run canary enable for 10% in 20m and monitor traces/allocs. Command:
  `POST /internal/config/rollouts -> selector=tier:standard,feature:streaming,percent:10`
ops-bot: Canary applied to 10% -> metric watches attached (p95, queue, upload-rate)
cheng_sre: currently p95 650ms, queues trending down. Hold 10m and decide.
lisa_support: prepping templated customer update to send after we stabilize with timeline and rollback instructions.
mike_oncall: check-in in 12m. If metrics hold, proceed with 50% then full. If regress, revert to off and open postmortem.
maya_eng: noted. will post rollback commands to this thread if needed. :thumbsup:
mike_oncall: thanks team. quick wins: (1) support advisory published, (2) streaming turned off for standard, (3) emergency throttle applied. Monitoring dashboards link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streams/incident-0063
incident-bot: INCIDENT 0063 status updated -> mitigation in place. Pager will stay active until resolution.
samir_prod: updating product and marketing leads now. I will also coordinate a short public note once we're green.
mike_oncall: closing loop: any blockers on support scripts? lisa_support?
lisa_support: none. playbook live in /docs/incidents/streaming-soft-stop.md. I'll start sending customer pings for enterprise that might be affected.
cheng_sre: good work. leaving watches on. will post if we see any backward pressure.
maya_eng: canary stable at 10% for 12m, p95=520ms, queues < 8. proceeding to 50%.
ops-bot: Canary -> 50% applied.
mike_oncall: after 50% hold looks good, we'll plan full re-enable. aim to finish within 90-120m if stable.
mike_oncall: final note: postmortem owners: maya_eng (engineer), cheng_sre (sre), lisa_support (customer comms). We will schedule follow-up retro.
incident-bot: INCIDENT 0063 mitigated -> streaming restored progressively. Please file postmortem under /postmortems/0063-streaming-soft-stop.json :white_check_mark:
